theme: Infer a reaction rate law from partial data
title: Catalytic Assay — recovering a saturating rate law from dilute-regime data
strategies: constant prediction (mean of the training rates) -> reproduces the checker's own baseline, ~0.1

greedy: first-order kinetics -- least-squares fit rate ~= a + b*S + c*C + d*S*C on the dilute training rows. Near-perfect on train (the true law is locally linear there), but the fit's implicit slope keeps growing with S forever; it overshoots catastrophically once S extrapolates past the training envelope into the regime where the true reaction saturates -- worst on the trap ids where the held-out gap is deepest

strong: the insight is that dividing by the catalyst level C collapses every regime onto ONE curve (rate/C is independent of C under the true law) -- pool that specific rate across ALL catalyst regimes, then profile-search the single saturation constant Km (with Vmax solved in closed form for each candidate Km) to fit the pooled curve. This exploits BOTH multi-regime consistency and the saturating functional form, and the recovered Vmax*C*S/(Km+S) generalises correctly into deep extrapolation and to catalyst levels never shown in training

headroom above strong: a nonlinear (non-grid) joint fit of Vmax and Km with proper heteroscedastic weighting, or pooling additional structure across near-degenerate regimes, can push held-out error closer to the assay's irreducible measurement-noise floor
